questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor. It accepts electrons and protons to form water; without this final acceptor, electron flow through the aerobic chain cannot continue normally.

options.text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor, accepts electrons and protons to form carbon dioxide, and allows electron flow continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor, accepts electrons and protons to form water, and allows electron flow continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor, accepts electrons and protons to form water, but electron flow cannot continue normally.
Oxygen is not the terminal electron acceptor, accepts electrons and protons to form water, and allows electron flow continue.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly explains oxygen's role at the end of the aerobic electron transport chain?

questions.explanation: Fermentation preserves glycolysis by regenerating NAD+. It uses no oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.

options.text: Fermentation replaces glycolysis, regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can keep running, uses no oxygen as terminal electron acceptor, and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
Fermentation does not replace glycolysis, regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can keep running, uses oxygen as terminal electron acceptor, and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
Fermentation does not replace glycolysis, regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can keep running, uses no oxygen as terminal electron acceptor, and produces more ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
